page.main:
Python

Use Python to read local data, build queries, and inspect or export results. Admitted queries run in ShardLoom. Unsupported work returns a diagnostic without fallback execution.

Run a local query
Section titled “Run a local query”

Create the small CSV in the getting-started walkthrough before running this example. The public run() report exposes the result and native execution evidence.

import shardloom as sl


ctx = sl.context()
result = (
    ctx.read("data/orders.csv")
       .filter(sl.col("status") == "paid")
       .limit(10)
       .run()
)


print(result.envelope.field_int("output_row_count"))
print(result.envelope.human_text)
print(result.fallback_attempted, result.external_engine_invoked)

ctx.read(path) infers local adapters for .csv, .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .parquet, .arrow, .ipc, .feather, .avro, .orc, and .vortex. CSV, flat JSON/JSONL/NDJSON, generated rows, and scoped local Vortex inputs are the default public examples. Parquet, Arrow IPC/Feather, Avro, and ORC are scoped local-format surfaces when the matching feature-gated build is present; otherwise ShardLoom returns deterministic adapter blockers without fallback execution.

Reuse And Export
Section titled “Reuse And Export”

Python contexts can retain a local worker to avoid per-call CLI startup. Automatic preparation reuses an unchanged source only when its schema and artifact identities match. Each query still has fresh execution state; a prepared artifact is not a cache of query results.

Admitted flat results can use write_vortex, write_parquet, write_arrow_ipc, write_avro, write_orc, write_csv, write_json, and write_jsonl through the shared native result and sink contracts. Feature gates, supported types, and result limits apply. See runtime and I/O and the user-surface index.

Consume results in batches
Section titled “Consume results in batches”

Current source builds add iter_batches() for admitted results and from_batches() for explicitly typed resident input. These additions merged in PR #1526 after complete local and hosted checks; published v0.4.0 packages predate them. Source builds now also admit opt-in streaming=True for one finite source used once through pure scan/filter/project operations, as below. Its corrected local acceptance and independent packet inspection pass. Final integration is tracked in PR #1530.

def orders():
    yield [{"order_id": 1, "amount": 12.5}]
    yield [{"order_id": 2, "amount": None}]


frame = sl.from_batches(
    orders, schema={"order_id": "int64", "amount": "float64"},
    streaming=True,
)
with frame.iter_batches(batch_rows=1024) as batches:
    for batch in batches:
        print(batch.result_rows)
    assert batches.report is not None

Input admits nullable Int64, finite Float64, booleans and UTF8 strings with an explicit schema. Each input batch contains at most 2,048 row mappings and an 8 MiB frame, with up to 128 fields and 4,096 batches per source. In the default resident mode (streaming=False), total native input must fit the query memory grant. A factory, as above, supplies fresh input for repeated calls; an iterable can be consumed once.

Streaming retains at most one native input batch, so cumulative input may exceed the query grant within those finite limits. It supports incremental results, bounded small collection or one native Vortex destination. Joins, repeated sources, sets, sorting, explicit limits/offsets, aggregates, windows and dynamic schemas reject before producer consumption. The producer must reach its explicit end event before results are final. Typed intake and output compaction are charged copies; output and sink reservations remain separate. No input spill or process-RSS ceiling is added. See the complete streaming contract for native intake, wire-frame, ownership and failure bounds.

Requesting the next result batch acknowledges the preceding one. Use the context manager when stopping early, and treat delivered batches as provisional until the final report is present after full exhaustion. Prepare compatibility file inputs explicitly to Vortex before batch consumption. See resource boundaries.

Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”

See the examples for preparation, bounded collection, writes, and blocker inspection. The limitations page describes current coverage gaps.

page.main:
Python

Use Python to read local data, build queries, and inspect or export results. Admitted queries run in ShardLoom. Unsupported work returns a diagnostic without fallback execution.

Run a local query
Section titled “Run a local query”

Create the small CSV in the getting-started walkthrough before running this example. The public run() report exposes the result and native execution evidence.

import shardloom as sl


ctx = sl.context()
result = (
    ctx.read("data/orders.csv")
       .filter(sl.col("status") == "paid")
       .limit(10)
       .run()
)


print(result.envelope.field_int("output_row_count"))
print(result.envelope.human_text)
print(result.fallback_attempted, result.external_engine_invoked)

ctx.read(path) infers local adapters for .csv, .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .parquet, .arrow, .ipc, .feather, .avro, .orc, and .vortex. CSV, flat JSON/JSONL/NDJSON, generated rows, and scoped local Vortex inputs are the default public examples. Parquet, Arrow IPC/Feather, Avro, and ORC are scoped local-format surfaces when the matching feature-gated build is present; otherwise ShardLoom returns deterministic adapter blockers without fallback execution.

Reuse And Export
Section titled “Reuse And Export”

Python contexts can retain a local worker to avoid per-call CLI startup. Automatic preparation reuses an unchanged source only when its schema and artifact identities match. Each query still has fresh execution state; a prepared artifact is not a cache of query results.

Admitted flat results can use write_vortex, write_parquet, write_arrow_ipc, write_avro, write_orc, write_csv, write_json, and write_jsonl through the shared native result and sink contracts. Feature gates, supported types, and result limits apply. See runtime and I/O and the user-surface index.

Consume results in batches
Section titled “Consume results in batches”

Current source builds add iter_batches() for admitted results and from_batches() for explicitly typed resident input. These additions merged in PR #1526 after complete local and hosted checks; published v0.4.0 packages predate them. Source builds now also admit opt-in streaming=True for one finite source used once through pure scan/filter/project operations, as below. Its corrected local acceptance and independent packet inspection pass. Final integration is tracked in PR #1530.

def orders():
    yield [{"order_id": 1, "amount": 12.5}]
    yield [{"order_id": 2, "amount": None}]


frame = sl.from_batches(
    orders, schema={"order_id": "int64", "amount": "float64"},
    streaming=True,
)
with frame.iter_batches(batch_rows=1024) as batches:
    for batch in batches:
        print(batch.result_rows)
    assert batches.report is not None

Input admits nullable Int64, finite Float64, booleans and UTF8 strings with an explicit schema. Each input batch contains at most 2,048 row mappings and an 8 MiB frame, with up to 128 fields and 4,096 batches per source. In the default resident mode (streaming=False), total native input must fit the query memory grant. A factory, as above, supplies fresh input for repeated calls; an iterable can be consumed once.

Streaming retains at most one native input batch, so cumulative input may exceed the query grant within those finite limits. It supports incremental results, bounded small collection or one native Vortex destination. Joins, repeated sources, sets, sorting, explicit limits/offsets, aggregates, windows and dynamic schemas reject before producer consumption. The producer must reach its explicit end event before results are final. Typed intake and output compaction are charged copies; output and sink reservations remain separate. No input spill or process-RSS ceiling is added. See the complete streaming contract for native intake, wire-frame, ownership and failure bounds.

Requesting the next result batch acknowledges the preceding one. Use the context manager when stopping early, and treat delivered batches as provisional until the final report is present after full exhaustion. Prepare compatibility file inputs explicitly to Vortex before batch consumption. See resource boundaries.

Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”

See the examples for preparation, bounded collection, writes, and blocker inspection. The limitations page describes current coverage gaps.

Failure and correction

The original hosted native Vortex job failed the existing malformed-metadata test when fsst-rs 0.6.0 asserted that the decoded allocation was smaller than its lower bound. A fixed all-escape stream reproduced the assertion locally against the old provider boundary; its nonzero exit and complete cleanup receipt are retained.

The existing feature-gated Vortex 0.85.0 provider remains the decoder. Before requesting its decoded payload, ShardLoom now walks each selected row's encoded codes and verifies that symbol expansion exactly matches the declared length. Each escape must contain its literal byte within that row, and every symbol reference must address a populated entry. Checking only the combined length would miss incorrect row boundaries and cross-row escapes.

"""Bind hosted checks and observed review/deployment state to the input source."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import json
import subprocess

import fsst_common as c

BASE = '0f7609daf7c4d062a0b939870803636d0c9b4ef8'
RUNTIME_COMMIT = 'b7de216fe421012d3f9b632ad19e95f19b88dbe5'
GH = '/opt/homebrew/bin/gh'
REPO = 'depsilon/shardloom'


def run(*command):
    return subprocess.check_output(command, cwd=c.ROOT, text=True, timeout=60).strip()


def pr(number):
    return json.loads(run(GH, 'pr', 'view', str(number), '--repo', REPO, '--json',
        'number,url,state,isDraft,headRefOid,baseRefOid,mergeCommit,mergedAt,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,reviews,comments'))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--stage', choices=('premerge', 'postmerge'), required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--attempt', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--head', required=True, help='Exact reviewed documentation/integration commit')

    parser.add_argument('--preview-url', required=True,
                        help='Observed deployed preview URL from the PR deployment comment')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    assert args.attempt > 0
    HEAD = args.head
    assert len(HEAD) == 40 and all(char in '0123456789abcdef' for char in HEAD)
    assert args.preview_url.startswith(('https://', 'http://'))
    observed = pr(1530)
    baseline = pr(1529)
    query = '''query { repository(owner: "depsilon", name: "shardloom") {
      pullRequest(number: 1530) {
        reviewThreads(first: 100) { nodes { id isResolved isOutdated
          comments(first: 100) { nodes { body url author { login } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage } }
        reviews(last: 100) { nodes { state body submittedAt commit { oid } author { login } }
          pageInfo { hasPreviousPage } }
        comments(last: 100) { nodes { id body url author { login } }
          pageInfo { hasPreviousPage } }
      }
    } }'''
    reviews = json.loads(run(GH, 'api', 'graphql', '-f', 'query=' + query))
    runs = json.loads(run(GH, 'api', 'repos/' + REPO
        + '/actions/runs?event=pull_request&head_sha=' + HEAD + '&per_page=100'))
    prefix = f'fsst-hosted-{args.stage}-{args.attempt}'
    snapshot = {'pr': observed, 'baseline_pr': baseline, 'reviews': reviews,
                'workflow_runs': runs, 'preview_url_argument': args.preview_url,
                'observed_at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
    c.write(c.OUT / (prefix + '-snapshot.json'), snapshot)

    assert not c.git('status', '--porcelain'), 'requires the clean tested tree'
    assert observed['headRefOid'] == HEAD and not observed['isDraft']
    assert baseline['state'] == 'MERGED' and baseline['mergeCommit']['oid'] == BASE
    expected = {row['name'] for row in baseline['statusCheckRollup']}
    assert len(expected) == 39
    for workflow in ('.github/workflows/ci.yml', '.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml'):
        assert c.git('show', BASE + ':' + workflow) == c.git('show', HEAD + ':' + workflow)
    checks = observed['statusCheckRollup']
    assert len(checks) == len(expected) and {row['name'] for row in checks} == expected
    assert all(row['status'] == 'COMPLETED' and row['conclusion'] == 'SUCCESS'
               for row in checks), [(row['name'], row['status'], row['conclusion'])
                                    for row in checks if row['conclusion'] != 'SUCCESS']
    assert runs['total_count'] == 2
    assert {row['name'] for row in runs['workflow_runs']} == {'CI', 'CodeQL Analysis'}
    assert all(row['head_sha'] == HEAD and row['status'] == 'completed'
               and row['conclusion'] == 'success' for row in runs['workflow_runs'])

    assert 'errors' not in reviews
    review = reviews['data']['repository']['pullRequest']
    assert not review['reviewThreads']['pageInfo']['hasNextPage']
    assert not review['reviews']['pageInfo']['hasPreviousPage']
    assert not review['comments']['pageInfo']['hasPreviousPage']
    assert not review['reviewThreads']['nodes'], 'new threads require primary inspection'
    assert not review['reviews']['nodes'], 'new reviews require primary inspection'
    review_summaries = [row for row in review['comments']['nodes']
                        if row['author']['login'] == 'chatgpt-codex-connector'
                        and '<!-- codex-pull-request-review-summary -->' in row['body']]
    assert len(review_summaries) == 1
    review_lines = [line for line in review_summaries[0]['body'].splitlines()
                    if '**Code Review**' in line]
    assert len(review_lines) == 1
    assert '✅ **Completed**' in review_lines[0] and f'`{HEAD[:7]}`' in review_lines[0]
    assert len(review['comments']['nodes']) == 2, 'new comments require primary inspection'
    deployment_comments = [row for row in review['comments']['nodes']
                           if row['author']['login'] == 'cloudflare-workers-and-pages'
                           and 'Deployment successful!' in row['body']]
    assert deployment_comments, 'observed preview deployment comment is required'
    assert any(args.preview_url in row['body'] and HEAD[:8] in row['body']
               for row in deployment_comments), 'preview URL must match the observed deployment comment'

    source = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-source-1.json')
    build = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-acceptance-build-1.json')
    acceptance = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-final-acceptance-1.json')
    assert c.source_hashes() == source['source_hashes'] and len(source['source_hashes']) == 947
    assert build['source_hashes'] == source['source_hashes']
    assert build['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert acceptance['status'] == 'passed_local_engine'
    assert acceptance['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert c.sha(build['binary']) == build['binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.OUT / acceptance['packet']) == acceptance['packet_sha256']

    index = c.read(c.ROOT / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-fsst-admission-2026-10-07.json')
    assert index['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME_COMMIT
    correction = index['integration_correction']
    assert correction['corrected_commit'] == RUNTIME_COMMIT
    assert correction['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert len(correction['changed_assets']) == 2 and correction['unchanged_assets'] == 945
    assert correction['old_bug_reproduced'] and correction['original_packet_preserved']
    original = c.ROOT / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-input-completion-2026-10-07.json.xz'
    assert c.sha(original) == correction['original_packet_sha256']
    assert index['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert index['acceptance']['packet_sha256'] == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['acceptance']['packet']) == index['acceptance']['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['portable_inspection']) == index['portable_inspection_sha256']
    assert index['documentation_updates_complete'] and not index['hosted_acceptance_complete']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance']) == index['documentation_acceptance_sha256']
    docs = c.read(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance'])
    assert docs['status'] == 'passed_local_documentation_acceptance'
    assert docs['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME_COMMIT
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / docs['archive']['path']) == docs['archive']['sha256']
    for name, identity in docs['source_files'].items():
        path = c.ROOT / name
        assert path.stat().st_size == identity['bytes']
        assert c.sha(path) == identity['sha256'], name
    search_path = c.ROOT / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-fsst-search-policy-2026-10-07.json'
    search = c.read(search_path)
    assert search['status'] == 'passed_local_search_policy_acceptance'
    assert search['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME_COMMIT
    assert search['runtime_source_assets_unchanged'] == 947
    assert search['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert search['original_documentation_receipt_sha256'] == index['documentation_acceptance_sha256']
    assert search['original_documentation_archive_sha256'] == docs['archive']['sha256']
    assert search['original_hosted_failure_preserved'] and search['temporary_preview_drained']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / search['archive']['path']) == search['archive']['sha256']
    assert search['archive']['all_members_reopened_and_hash_checked']
    assert len(search['source_files']) == 6
    for name, identity in search['source_files'].items():
        assert (c.ROOT / name).stat().st_size == identity['bytes']
        assert c.sha(c.ROOT / name) == identity['sha256'], name
    browser = search['browser']
    assert browser['status'] == 'passed_search_with_actual_deployment_headers'
    assert '4 results for streaming' in browser['search_state']
    assert browser['landed']['url'].endswith('/python-surface/#consume-results-in-batches')
    assert not browser['console_warnings_errors']
    preview_path = c.OUT / 'fsst-hosted-preview-2.json'
    preview = c.read(preview_path)
    assert preview['status'] == 'passed_hosted_search_and_guide' and preview['head'] == HEAD
    assert preview['origin'] == args.preview_url
    assert preview['page']['url'] == args.preview_url + '/field-guide/python-surface/#consume-results-in-batches'
    assert preview['page']['viewport'] == preview['page']['body']
    assert '4 results for streaming' in preview['search_state']
    assert not preview['console_warnings_errors']
    assert not index['broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete']
    assert not index['package_publication_performed']
    assert not index['performance_claim_allowed']
    if args.stage == 'premerge':
        assert observed['state'] == 'OPEN' and observed['mergeStateStatus'] == 'CLEAN'
        assert observed['baseRefOid'] == BASE and c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == HEAD
        assert c.git('ls-remote', '--heads', 'origin', 'main').split()[0] == BASE
        merge = None
    else:
        assert observed['state'] == 'MERGED' and observed['mergedAt']
        merge = observed['mergeCommit']['oid']
        assert c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == merge
        assert c.git('rev-list', '--parents', '-n', '1', merge).split() == [merge, BASE, HEAD]
        assert c.git('rev-parse', merge + '^{tree}') == c.git('rev-parse', HEAD + '^{tree}')
        assert c.git('ls-remote', '--heads', 'origin', 'main').split()[0] == merge
    result = {
        'status': 'passed_' + args.stage,
        'pr': 1530,
        'head': HEAD,
        'base': BASE,
        'baseline_pr': 1529,
        'merge_commit': merge,
        'successful_hosted_checks': len(checks),
        'hosted_check_names': sorted(expected),
        'runtime_commit': RUNTIME_COMMIT,
        'runtime_source_assets_verified': 947,
        'runtime_source_assets_unchanged_from_corrected_runtime': True,
        'original_runtime_assets_changed_for_correction': 2,
        'original_runtime_assets_unchanged_after_correction': 945,
        'original_acceptance_packet_preserved_sha256': correction['original_packet_sha256'],
        'source_identity_sha256': source['source_identity_sha256'],
        'runtime_binary_sha256': acceptance['binary_sha256'],
        'acceptance_packet_sha256': acceptance['packet_sha256'],
        'documentation_archive_sha256': docs['archive']['sha256'],
        'search_policy_receipt_sha256': c.sha(search_path),
        'search_policy_archive_sha256': search['archive']['sha256'],
        'local_search_with_deployment_headers_passed': True,
        'hosted_preview_search_passed': True,
        'hosted_preview_browser_sha256': c.sha(preview_path),
        'snapshot_sha256': c.sha(c.OUT / (prefix + '-snapshot.json')),
        'local_engine_acceptance_sha256': c.sha(c.OUT / 'fsst-final-acceptance-1.json'),
        'observed_preview_url': args.preview_url,
        'review_state': 'no_new_submitted_reviews_or_threads_observed',
        'automated_review_completion': 'observed_in_head_bound_summary',
        'hosted_automated_review': 'completed_no_posted_findings',
        'submitted_approval_inferred': False,
        'broader_roadmap_complete': False,
        'package_publication_attempted': False,
        'driver_sha256': c.sha(__file__),
    }
    c.write(c.OUT / (prefix + '.json'), result)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import hashlib
import json
import subprocess

import fsst_common as c

HEAD = '24bd2e5bd7e2eae67a5b39d90777e46bcd71f9d0'
BASE = '0f7609daf7c4d062a0b939870803636d0c9b4ef8'

def main():

    post = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-hosted-postmerge-1.json')
    assert pre['status'] == 'passed_premerge' and post['status'] == 'passed_postmerge'
    assert pre['head'] == post['head'] == HEAD
    assert pre['base'] == post['base'] == BASE
    assert pre['baseline_pr'] == post['baseline_pr'] == 1529
    assert pre['successful_hosted_checks'] == post['successful_hosted_checks'] == 39
    assert pre['hosted_check_names'] == post['hosted_check_names']
    assert pre['hosted_automated_review'] == post['hosted_automated_review'] == 'completed_no_posted_findings'
    assert not pre['submitted_approval_inferred'] and not post['submitted_approval_inferred']
    merge = post['merge_commit']
    assert c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == merge and not c.git('status', '--porcelain')
    assert c.git('rev-list', '--parents', '-n', '1', merge).split() == [merge, BASE, HEAD]
    assert c.git('rev-parse', HEAD + '^{tree}') == c.git('rev-parse', merge + '^{tree}')
    source = c.frozen()
    acceptance = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-final-acceptance-1.json')
    build = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-acceptance-build-1.json')
    assert len(source['source_hashes']) == 947 and build['source_hashes'] == source['source_hashes']
    assert acceptance['status'] == 'passed_local_engine'
    assert pre['runtime_commit'] == post['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME
    assert pre['source_identity_sha256'] == post['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert c.sha(build['binary']) == build['binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert pre['runtime_binary_sha256'] == post['runtime_binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.OUT / acceptance['packet']) == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    for stage, record in (('premerge', pre), ('postmerge', post)):
        assert c.sha(c.OUT / f'fsst-hosted-{stage}-1-snapshot.json') == record['snapshot_sha256']
    index = c.read(EVIDENCE / 'native-fsst-admission-2026-10-07.json')
    assert index['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME
    assert index['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert index['documentation_updates_complete'] and not index['hosted_acceptance_complete']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['acceptance']['packet']) == index['acceptance']['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['portable_inspection']) == index['portable_inspection_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance']) == index['documentation_acceptance_sha256']
    docs = c.read(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance'])
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / docs['archive']['path']) == docs['archive']['sha256']
    for name, identity in docs['source_files'].items():
        assert (c.ROOT / name).stat().st_size == identity['bytes']
        assert c.sha(c.ROOT / name) == identity['sha256']
    search_path = EVIDENCE / 'native-fsst-search-policy-2026-10-07.json'
    search = c.read(search_path)
    assert search['status'] == 'passed_local_search_policy_acceptance'
    assert pre['search_policy_receipt_sha256'] == post['search_policy_receipt_sha256'] == c.sha(search_path)
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / search['archive']['path']) == search['archive']['sha256']
    assert pre['search_policy_archive_sha256'] == post['search_policy_archive_sha256'] == search['archive']['sha256']
    for name, identity in search['source_files'].items():
        assert (c.ROOT / name).stat().st_size == identity['bytes']
        assert c.sha(c.ROOT / name) == identity['sha256']
    correction = index['integration_correction']
    assert len(correction['changed_assets']) == 2 and correction['unchanged_assets'] == 945
    assert c.sha(EVIDENCE / 'native-input-completion-2026-10-07.json.xz') == correction['original_packet_sha256']
    assert not index['broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete']
    assert not index['package_publication_performed'] and not index['performance_claim_allowed']

    preview_path = c.OUT / 'fsst-hosted-preview-2.json'
    preview = c.read(preview_path)
    production = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-hosted-production-1.json')
    link = c.read(c.OUT / 'fsst-hosted-production-link-1.json')
    assert preview['head'] == HEAD and production['merge_commit'] == merge
    assert preview['origin'] == pre['observed_preview_url']
    assert pre['hosted_preview_browser_sha256'] == post['hosted_preview_browser_sha256'] == c.sha(preview_path)
    assert production['origin'] == 'https://shardloom.io'
    for page in (preview, production):
        assert page['status'] == 'passed_hosted_search_and_guide'
        assert page['page']['url'] == page['origin'] + '/field-guide/python-surface/#consume-results-in-batches'
        assert page['page']['viewport'] == page['page']['body']
        assert '4 results for streaming' in page['search_state']
        assert not page['console_warnings_errors']
        assert page['page']['acceptance_link'] == 'https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/' + REPORT
    assert preview['page']['main'] == production['page']['main']
    assert link['url'] == production['page']['acceptance_link']
    assert link['status'] == 'passed_merged_report_link'
    assert 'FSST admission correction and input acceptance' in link['body'] and '27,373' in link['body']

    report_bytes = subprocess.check_output([
        '/opt/homebrew/bin/gh', 'api', 'repos/depsilon/shardloom/contents/' + REPORT,
        '-f', 'ref=' + merge, '-X', 'GET', '-H', 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json',
    ], cwd=c.ROOT, timeout=45)
    assert report_bytes == (c.ROOT / REPORT).read_bytes()
    report = report_bytes.decode()
    assert RUNTIME in report and '27,373' in report and '129' in report
    assert '1e-12' in report and 'RSS' in report and 'hosted' in report
    checks = json.loads(subprocess.check_output([
        '/opt/homebrew/bin/gh', 'api', 'repos/depsilon/shardloom/commits/' + merge
        + '/check-runs?per_page=100',
    ], cwd=c.ROOT, text=True, timeout=45))
    deployments = [row for row in checks['check_runs'] if row['name'] == 'Workers Builds: shardloom']
    assert len(deployments) == 1
    deployment = deployments[0]
    assert deployment['head_sha'] == merge and deployment['status'] == 'completed'
    assert deployment['conclusion'] == 'success'
    deployment_path = c.OUT / 'fsst-production-deployment-1.json'
    if deployment_path.exists():
        assert c.read(deployment_path) == deployment
    else:
        c.write(deployment_path, deployment)

    names = [
        'fsst-hosted-premerge-1.json', 'fsst-hosted-premerge-1-snapshot.json',
        'fsst-hosted-postmerge-1.json', 'fsst-hosted-postmerge-1-snapshot.json',
        'fsst-hosted-preview-2.json', 'fsst-hosted-production-1.json',
        'fsst-hosted-production-link-1.json', 'fsst-production-deployment-1.json',
        'fsst-hosted-preview-headers-probe-failure-1.json',
        'verify_fsst_hosted.py', 'build_fsst_hosted_receipt.py',
    ]
    records = []
    for name in names:
        data = (c.OUT / name).read_bytes()
        records.append({'name': name, 'bytes': len(data),
                        'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                        'contents': json.loads(data) if name.endswith('.json') else data.decode()})
    images = []
    for surface, page in (('preview', preview), ('production', production)):
        for number, name in enumerate(page['screenshots'], 1):
            original = c.OUT / name
            target = EVIDENCE / f'native-fsst-{surface}-{number}-2026-10-07.jpg'
            with target.open('xb') as stream:
                stream.write(original.read_bytes())
            assert c.sha(original) == c.sha(target)
            images.append({'path': target.name, 'bytes': target.stat().st_size, 'sha256': c.sha(target)})
    record = {
        'schema_version': 'shardloom.native_input_fsst_hosted_acceptance.v1',
        'status': 'passed_hosted_integration',
        'pr_url': 'https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/pull/1530',
        'head': HEAD, 'merge_commit': merge, 'successful_pr_checks': 39,
        'merge_tree_equals_accepted_head': True,
        'runtime_commit': RUNTIME, 'runtime_source_assets_verified': 947,
        'runtime_source_assets_unchanged': True,
        'source_identity_sha256': source['source_identity_sha256'],
        'runtime_binary_sha256': acceptance['binary_sha256'],
        'original_runtime_assets_changed_for_correction': 2,
        'original_runtime_assets_unchanged_after_correction': 945,
        'original_packet_preserved_sha256': correction['original_packet_sha256'],
        'review': 'Primary review and complete corrected local acceptance preceded merge. Automated review completed for the accepted head with no posted findings. No submitted approval is inferred.',
        'website': 'Preview and merged production browser search both returned four results and opened the batch guide without console warnings or errors. The complete rendered guide text matches; its acceptance link opens the merged report. Exact report bytes also match the accepted source. Historical hosted-pending status prose is preserved in the original acceptance record.',
        'http_probe_boundary': 'A separate urllib request to the preview returned HTTP 403. It provides no deployed-header byte proof. Ordinary browser functional checks passed; local response-header and policy regression checks are preserved in the search supplement.',
        'search_policy_evidence': {'path': str(search_path.relative_to(c.ROOT)), 'sha256': c.sha(search_path)},
        'report_identity': {'path': REPORT, 'commit': merge, 'bytes': len(report_bytes),
                            'sha256': hashlib.sha256(report_bytes).hexdigest()},
        'temporary_tabs_closed': True, 'package_publication_attempted': False,
        'broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete': False,
        'process_rss_cap_claim': False, 'broad_engine_speedup_claim': False,
        'records': records, 'images': images,
    }
    serialized = json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n'
    assert '/' + 'Users' + '/' not in serialized and '/' + 'home' + '/' not in serialized
    target = EVIDENCE / 'native-fsst-hosted-2026-10-07.json'
    with target.open('x') as stream:
        stream.write(serialized)
    assert c.read(target) == record
    print(json.dumps({'status': record['status'], 'sha256': c.sha(target),
                      'bytes': target.stat().st_size, 'records': len(records), 'images': len(images)}), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
